lesson.title: M4 · Soft margin: hinge loss and objective
lesson.lead: Priority 1. 18 marks: Sep 2025 Q5 (7), Mar 2026 Q6 (7), 2023 regular Q2C (2), 2023 DS makeup Q2C (2).

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: P1 and M1 only: the constraint yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1 and reading the sign of wᵀx + b. No dual or kernels.

**They give:** 4 labelled points, C, and one or two proposed (w, b). **They ask:** the soft-margin problem with slacks, its unconstrained hinge form, yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) for each point, the hinge loss per point, the total objective, which model is better, and which points are margin errors.
min ½‖w‖² + C·Σ ξᵢ   s.t.  yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1 − ξᵢ,  ξᵢ ≥ 0
blocks.caption: Soft-margin primal: one constraint pair per point

blocks.text: ξᵢ = max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b))  ⇒  min ½‖w‖² + C·Σ max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b))
blocks.caption: Why the two forms are the same (Mar 2026 Q6b, 2 marks): at the optimum each slack is as small as both constraints allow

items: Make a table: point, yᵢ, wᵀxᵢ + b, yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b), hinge loss.
Margin term: ½‖w‖² (e.g. w = (1, 1) gives 1).
Total = ½‖w‖² + C × (sum of hinge losses). The smaller total is the better model.
Read each point: yf ≥ 1 is correct and outside the margin (loss 0); 0 < yf < 1 is correct but inside the margin (a **margin error**); yf ≤ 0 is misclassified (loss ≥ 1).

blocks.label: The repeated 2-mark part
blocks.text: Given (y, y′) = (0.5, 1) and (1, −1): hinge = max(0, 1 − y·y′) = 0.5 and 2. The second has y·y′ < 0, so it is the misclassified sample.

blocks.label: Exam trap
blocks.text: A point with loss 0.5 is **correctly classified**. Only yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≤ 0 means misclassified.

items: Saurabh sir: **P48** (slacks, hinge, effect of C), **Companion Q11** (slacks and a failed candidate), **Lecture 15** slide example (4 points, C = 0.5).

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 60 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_15.pdf` p. 23–26 (worked soft-margin problem, C = 0.5); SVM Companion §10.1–10.3 and §10.5 (slack, the C penalty, hinge loss falls out of the slack).
**Do:** P48, Companion Q11, then Mar 2026 Q6 and Sep 2025 Q5 timed.
**Video, only if stuck:** [Soft margin SVMs: the loss-function approach](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=28rKRHNAhvM), only if ξᵢ = max(0, 1 − yᵢf(xᵢ)) doesn't click.

lesson.lead: Priority 8. Sep 2024 makeup Q(A) (5 × 1 mark). Short answers with a sketch.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: M4 (hinge loss, slacks) and the idea of a support vector from M2.

items: A mislabelled point that is not a support vector does not move the boundary. A mislabelled support vector does.
αᵢ = 0: not a support vector. 0 < αᵢ < C: free support vector on the margin (use it to compute b). αᵢ = C: bounded support vector, inside the margin or misclassified.
Saurabh sir: **Companion Q16** (read a trained model from its α's), plus the C part of **P48**.

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 20 min)

items: **Read:** SVM Companion §9.1 (the three regions: α = 0, 0 < α < C, α = C) and §10.4 (reading C: big fine vs small fine).
**Do:** Companion Q16, then Sep 2024 makeup Q(A).
**Video, only if stuck:** No video: the slides and the companion cover it.

lesson.title: M2 · Support vectors and boundary from tiny data
lesson.lead: Priority 7. 2023 DS makeup Q2A (5 marks). Saurabh sir has 6 problems on it.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: M1. P2 only if the question asks you to prove the answer with KKT.

items: Plot the points. Guess the support vectors: the closest points of opposite classes.
The boundary is halfway between them, perpendicular to the line joining them (for one pair).
Prove the guess with KKT: the support vectors satisfy yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) = 1, every other point gives > 1, and all α ≥ 0.
Removing a point that is not a support vector does not change the boundary. Removing a support vector can.

blocks.label: Companion Q10 trap
blocks.text: A point lying exactly on a margin line can still have α = 0, so it is **not** necessarily a support vector.

items: Saurabh sir: **P45** (1-D hard margin via KKT), **Companion Q6** (1-D, adding a point), **Q8** (two points from scratch), **Q9** (five points on a line), **Q10** (the trap), **KKT set P15** (capstone).

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 40 min)

items: **Read:** SVM Companion §9 (the three regions, sparsity, the prediction rule).
**Do:** P45, Companion Q8, Q9, Q10 (the trap), then 2023 DS makeup Q2A.
**Video, only if stuck:** No video: the slides and the companion cover it. Needs P2 only for KKT proofs.

lesson.title: M3 · Solve or reason with the dual
lesson.lead: Priority 6. 11 marks: 2022 regular Q1c (8), Sep 2024 regular Q(A) (3). Not in the last three papers, but 8 marks when it comes.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: M1 (the primal) and P2 (Lagrangian, KKT), plus partial derivatives.
max Σ αᵢ − ½ ΣΣ αᵢαⱼ yᵢyⱼ (xᵢᵀxⱼ)   s.t.  Σ αᵢyᵢ = 0,  αᵢ ≥ 0
blocks.caption: With a kernel, replace xᵢᵀxⱼ by k(xᵢ, xⱼ)

items: Use Σ αᵢyᵢ = 0 to remove one α, so the dual has the fewest variables (2022 asks exactly this).
Set the partial derivatives to 0 and solve for the α's.
Check every αᵢ ≥ 0. If one is negative, that point is not a support vector: set its α to 0 and solve again.
w = Σ αᵢyᵢxᵢ, then b from any support vector: yₛ(wᵀxₛ + b) = 1.

blocks.label: Sep 2024 theory part (3 marks)
blocks.text: Adding a point: the old optimal α's with αₙ₊₁ = 0 are still feasible for the new problem, so the new optimum is at least the old one.

items: Saurabh sir: **P47** (solve the dual for three points), **Companion Q3** (full dual solve, b ≠ 0), **Q4** (solver-given α's), **Q14** (work backwards from the α's).

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 60 min)

items: **Read:** SVM Companion §7–8 (differentiate L with respect to w and b, strong duality as a free check); `Lecture_15.pdf` p. 3–16 (primal to dual).
**Do:** P47, Companion Q3 and Q14, then 2022 regular Q1c (8 marks).
**Video, only if stuck:** [SVMs: solving using Lagrange](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PGYnwSwKuRo), only if the step from the primal to Σα − ½ΣΣ… is unclear.

worked.title: Hard margin · 2023 DS makeup Q2A: support vectors from seven points (5 marks)

problem.text: Positive: (2, 2), (4, 3), (5, 3), (5, 6). Negative: (−1, −1), (−3, −3), (−4, −2). (i) Find the support vectors. Is the data linearly separable? [1M] (ii) Find the decision boundary. [3M] (iii) What happens to the boundary if (2, 2) is removed? [1M]

steps.label: (i) Closest pair
steps.text: The nearest positive–negative pair is (2, 2) and (−1, −1) (distance √18). Every other pair is farther. So the support vectors are **(2, 2) and (−1, −1)**, and the data is linearly separable (the line below separates it).

steps.label: (ii) Geometry
steps.text: With one support vector per class, the boundary is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Midpoint (0.5, 0.5), direction (1, 1) ⇒ **x₁ + x₂ = 1**.

steps.label: (ii) Canonical w, b
steps.text: Scale so the support vectors give ±1: f(x) = (x₁ + x₂ − 1)/3, so w = (⅓, ⅓), b = −⅓. Check: (2, 2) → 1, (−1, −1) → −1. Margin 1/‖w‖ = 3/√2 ≈ 2.12.

steps.label: (ii) Check the rest
steps.text: (4, 3): 2, (5, 3): 2.33, (5, 6): 3.33 (all > 1); (−3, −3): −2.33, (−4, −2): −2.33 (all < −1). No other point is inside the margin, so this is the SVM boundary.

steps.label: (iii) Remove (2, 2)
steps.text: (2, 2) is a support vector, so removing it **changes the boundary**: it moves towards the positive class and the margin gets wider. Removing a non-support vector (e.g. (5, 6)) would change nothing.

worked.answer: Support vectors (2, 2) and (−1, −1); boundary x₁ + x₂ = 1 (w = (⅓, ⅓), b = −⅓); removing (2, 2) moves the boundary.

worked.title: Dual · 2022 regular Q1c: the dual in two variables (8 marks)

problem.text: Points (x, y, class): (−1, 3, +), (1, 3, −), (−1, 1, −). With multipliers α₁, α₂, α₃, set up the Lagrangian dual in the fewest variables and terms, and find the optimal hyperplane by calculus.

steps.label: Dual objective
steps.text:
L = Σαᵢ − ½ΣΣ αᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼ(xᵢ·xⱼ). Dot products: x₁·x₁ = 10, x₂·x₂ = 10, x₃·x₃ = 2, x₁·x₂ = 8, x₁·x₃ = 4, x₂·x₃ = 2. y = (+1, −1, −1).
L = α₁ + α₂ + α₃ − ½(10α₁² + 10α₂² + 2α₃² − 16α₁α₂ − 8α₁α₃ + 4α₂α₃). [3M]

steps.label: Remove α₁
steps.text: Σαᵢyᵢ = 0 ⇒ α₁ = α₂ + α₃. Substituting and simplifying gives **L = −2α₂² − 2α₃² + 2α₂ + 2α₃** (two variables, four terms). [2M]

steps.label: Check
steps.text: (1, 3): −1 + 3 − 3 = −1 ✓. (−1, 1): 1 + 1 − 3 = −1 ✓. All three are support vectors.

worked.title: Dual · Sep 2024 regular Q(A): adding a point can't lower the optimum (3 marks)

problem.text: Problem (A) is the usual hard-margin dual on n points. Problem (B) adds a point xₙ₊₁ = ½(xᵢ + xⱼ) for two points of the same class, with yₙ₊₁ = yᵢ. Show the optimal value of (B) is ≥ the optimal value of (A).

steps.label: Feasible point for (B)
steps.text: Take the optimum of (A), (α₁*, …, αₙ*), and set αₙ₊₁ = 0. Both constraints of (B) hold: Σαᵢyᵢ = 0 (the new term is 0) and every α ≥ 0.

steps.label: Same value
steps.text: Every term in (B)'s objective that is new contains αₙ₊₁ = 0, so this feasible point gives exactly O_A.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.text: The optimum of a maximisation problem is ≥ the value at any feasible point, so **O_B ≥ O_A**.

worked.answer: (α*, 0) is feasible for (B) with value O_A, so the maximum of (B) is at least O_A.
worked.priorityWhy: Asked twice: previous batch (Apr 2023) Q1 and Sep 2024 regular Q(A)

worked.title: Soft margin · Mar 2026 Q6: hinge form and total objective (7 marks)

problem.text: X1 (3, 3) +1, X2 (5, 5) +1, X3 (3, 0) −1, X4 (5, 0) −1. (a) Soft-margin primal with slacks ξᵢ and C. [1M] (b) Show it equals min ½‖w‖² + CΣmax(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b)). [2M] (c) For w = (1, −1), b = 0: yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) for each point [2M], hinge loss of each [1M], total objective for C = 1 [1M].

steps.label: (a) Primal
steps.text: min ½(w₁² + w₂²) + C(ξ₁ + ξ₂ + ξ₃ + ξ₄) s.t. 3w₁ + 3w₂ + b ≥ 1 − ξ₁, 5w₁ + 5w₂ + b ≥ 1 − ξ₂, −(3w₁ + b) ≥ 1 − ξ₃, −(5w₁ + b) ≥ 1 − ξ₄, ξᵢ ≥ 0.

steps.label: (b) Hinge form
steps.text: The constraint gives ξᵢ ≥ 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b), and also ξᵢ ≥ 0 [1M]. The objective wants ξᵢ as small as possible, so ξᵢ = max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b)): the hinge loss. Substituting gives the unconstrained form [1M].

worked.title: Soft margin · Sep 2025 Q5: which of two models is better (7 marks)

problem.text: x₁ (0, 0) −1, x₂ (2, 2) +1, x₃ (2, 0) −1, x₄ (0, 2) +1; C = 1. Model A: w = (1, 1), b = −1.5. Model B: w = (1, −1), b = 0. (a) ½‖w‖² for each. [1M] (b) Hinge loss of each point and the sum. [3M] (c) Total objective; which model is better? [1M] (d) For the better model: margin errors and correctly classified points. [2M]

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: A: 1 + 2 = **3**. B: 1 + 8 = **9**. Model A is better (smaller objective).

steps.label: (d) Read model A
steps.text: x₁ (yf = 1.5) and x₂ (2.5): correct and outside the margin. x₄ (0.5): correct but **inside the margin**, a margin error. x₃ (−0.5): **misclassified** (also a margin error). Correctly classified: x₁, x₂, x₄.

worked.answer: Objectives A = 3, B = 9, so A is better; in A, x₃ is misclassified and x₄ is a margin error; x₁, x₂, x₄ are correctly classified.

worked.title: Soft margin · 2023 Q2C: hinge loss of two samples (2 marks)

problem.text: Samples (y, y′): (0.5, 1) and (1, −1), where y′ is the prediction. Find the hinge loss of each and say which is misclassified.

steps.label: Formula
steps.text: Hinge loss = max(0, 1 − y·y′).

steps.label: Misclassified
steps.text: Sample 2: y·y′ = −1 < 0 (opposite signs). Sample 1 has a non-zero loss but y·y′ > 0, so it is correct, just inside the margin.

worked.answer: 0.5 and 2; the second sample is misclassified.

worked.title: Soft margin · Sep 2024 makeup Q(A): small C versus large C (5 marks)

problem.text: Noisy-sensor data in two classes, SVM with a quadratic kernel and parameter C. (a) Sketch a boundary for small C. (b) For large C. (c) Mark a point whose wrong label would not affect the boundary. (d) One whose wrong label would. (e) High or low C for this data? [1M each]

steps.label: (a) Small C
steps.text: Violations are cheap: a smooth boundary with a wide margin that lets a few points sit inside it or on the wrong side.

steps.label: (b) Large C
steps.text: Violations are expensive: a tighter, wigglier boundary that tries to classify every point correctly, with a narrow margin. Mark some support vectors.

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: Any point that is **not** a support vector (far from the boundary, α = 0). Its label does not enter w.

steps.label: (d)
steps.text: Any **support vector** (on or inside the margin). Changing its label changes the solution.

steps.label: (e)
steps.text: The data is noisy, so allow some misclassification: **low C**.

worked.answer: Small C: wide, smooth margin; large C: narrow, tight fit; non-support vectors don't matter, support vectors do; choose low C for noisy data.

blocks.text: min ½‖w‖² + C·Σ max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b))

flashcards.back: A training point with αᵢ > 0. For hard margin it lies on a margin line, yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) = 1. Removing it can move the boundary.

flashcards.front: Is every point on the margin line a support vector?
flashcards.back: No. A point can sit exactly on the margin line with α = 0 (Companion Q10).
Correct, but inside the margin (a margin error). Hinge loss 0.5.

flashcards.front: Noisy data: small or large C?
flashcards.back: Small C: wider margin, tolerates a few violations.

flashcards.back: w = Σαᵢyᵢxᵢ; b from any support vector: yₛ(wᵀxₛ + b) = 1.

quiz.q: w = (1, 1), b = −1.5. Hinge loss of x = (2, 0) with y = −1?
A point has yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) = 0.3. It is…
quiz.explain: Positive means correct; below 1 means inside the margin.

quiz.q: Which points determine w in an SVM?
quiz.explain: w = Σαᵢyᵢxᵢ and α = 0 for every other point.

formulas.name: Soft-margin primal
formulas.formula: min ½‖w‖² + C·Σξᵢ  s.t.  yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1 − ξᵢ, ξᵢ ≥ 0

formulas.name: Hinge form
formulas.formula: min ½‖w‖² + C·Σ max(0, 1 − yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b))

formulas.name: Hinge loss of one point
formulas.note: 0 outside the margin, between 0 and 1 inside it, ≥ 1 when misclassified

formulas.name: Dual
formulas.formula: max Σαᵢ − ½ΣΣ αᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼ k(xᵢ, xⱼ)  s.t.  Σαᵢyᵢ = 0, 0 ≤ αᵢ (≤ C for soft margin)

formulas.name: From α to w and b
formulas.formula: w = Σ αᵢyᵢxᵢ,  b = yₛ − wᵀxₛ for a support vector xₛ
